feature: Center on the Artboard, Union and Outline Stroke
summary: The three dots on the Layers header now carry the icon mock's last three rows: Center on the Artboard puts what is picked in the middle of its frame, Union joins picked shapes into one path (Option Command U), and Outline Stroke turns a shape's line into a filled shape of its own (Shift Command O). Each is also in the Layer menu and on a shape's right-click menu under the same name.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: layers-menu-icon-rows-walk and layers-menu-icon-rows-right-click-walk.

try.do: Layer > New Frame, pick 24 in Icons, Add Frame, then draw an oval near the frame's top left corner and open the three dots on the Layers header.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.
Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command Z, draw a box overlapping the oval, pick both rows and press Option Command U.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Tick Outline on the joined path in Appearance, set its Thickness to 1, and press Shift Command O.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag one of the new outline's points: the ring reshapes and the fill under it stays.
Press Command Z, then right click the shape and choose Outline Stroke.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick a filled box drawn with the box tool and add a Border in Effects, then choose Outline Stroke: the Border becomes the outline layer.

evaluate: When a shape has both a fill and a line, is a new 'outline' layer above the fill what you expected, rather than one shape?
Should Center on the Artboard move several picked shapes together as one drawing (it does now), or centre each one on its own?
Is it right that Union is both its own row with a key and Join inside Combine Shapes, or is one of them enough?
Is Center on the Artboard without a key fine, given Option Command C stays Canvas Size?
rough: The mock prints Center on the artboard on Option Command C; that is Canvas Size, and keys follow Photoshop (your call on 2026-07-05), so the row has no key, as this task's acceptance allows.

The mock's Union stays live with the four shapes kept underneath; Union here is Join, which makes one path with real points, the answer already settled in two-shapes-become-one-join-them-cut-one-out-keep.
Rows read in Title Case (Center on the Artboard, Outline Stroke) where the mock writes sentence case, per UX-PATTERNS §7 'How a menu row is capitalised'.
The panel menu's glyphs are system symbols chosen to look like the mock's union, flatten and align icons, the same way Mirror's row was matched, per UX-PATTERNS §8; they are close, not identical.
Make Component and Hide This Panel stay below the new rows: they come from components.html's drawing of the same menu, which the icon mock does not show.
A shape drawn with the oval or box tool arrives filled with no line, so Outline Stroke is dimmed until a line is added (Outline in Appearance on a path, or a Border on a box or oval).
On a small shape a thick line fills it completely; outlining it then gives a solid shape the size of the fill, which is the same picture but can look like nothing happened.
Not offered on a video, like Mirror Across Center beside it.
